bibl.title: Putting Fear in Its Place: Remapping of Hippocampal Place Cells during Fear Conditioning

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether learning to fear a place changes the hippocampal map of that place, with the place itself unchanged
span.quote: However, the causes and functional purpose of such remapping are poorly understood. In the present study, we addressed this question by investigating whether aversive conditioning induces place cell remapping.

span.label: whether aversive conditioning induces place cell remapping, and whether the amount of remapping tracks what the animal learned rather than what it was shown
span.quote: Furthermore, contextual fear conditioning caused significantly more remapping of place cells than auditory fear conditioning, suggesting that place cell remapping was related to the rat's learned fear of the environment. These results suggest that one possible function of place cell remapping may be to generate new spatial representations of a single environment, which could help the animal to discriminate among different motivational contexts within that environment.

span.label: shows fear conditioning remaps place cells in the training environment but not a control environment, and remaps more when the context rather than a tone predicts shock
span.quote: We recorded hippocampal place cells in two spatial environments: a training environment in which rats underwent fear conditioning and a neutral control environment. Fear conditioning caused many place cells to alter (or remap) their preferred firing locations in the training environment, whereas most cells remained stable in the control environment. This finding indicates that aversive reinforcement can induce place cell remapping even when the environment itself remains unchanged.

span.label: existence
span.quote: This finding indicates that aversive reinforcement can induce place cell remapping even when the environment itself remains unchanged.

span.label: hippocampal place cell remapping during fear conditioning
span.quote: We recorded hippocampal place cells in two spatial environments: a training environment in which rats underwent fear conditioning and a neutral control environment.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Rats that were chronically implanted with hippocampal recording electrodes were placed in an experimental chamber in which they foraged for small food pellets dropped from an overhead dispenser ( Muller et al., 1987 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A change in the motivational valence of the environment triggers re-representation: the hippocampus rewrites its map so that the previously learned appetitive associations no longer attach to it, letting new aversive associations form on a fresh representation
span.quote: One possibility would be to alter the hippocampal representation of the environment itself, so that the previously learned appetitive associations would no longer be in force.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Recoding the environment reduces competition between appetitive and aversive motivational drives that would arise if one representation carried both valences
span.quote: This may help to reduce competition between different motivational drives that might otherwise occur if a single environmental representation were permitted to acquire both appetitive and aversive motivational valence.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Remapping is driven by predictive relevance rather than sensory input: cells remap when the environment itself is the best predictor of the reinforcer, because more remapped cells are then needed to carry the new contextual association
span.quote: This suggests that place cells are most likely to remap an environment in which aversive reinforcement occurs when the environment itself is the best predictor of reinforcement, which provides circumstantial evidence for the hypothesis that cells that remap are more involved in acquiring the new contextual association than non-remapping cells, because the demand for such cells would be greater during context conditioning than cue conditioning.

span.label: an environment that predicted food now predicts shock, and re-representing it lets aversive associations form without competing with the appetitive ones
span.quote: One possibility would be to alter the hippocampal representation of the environment itself, so that the previously learned appetitive associations would no longer be in force. Aversive associations could then quickly be formed with the new hippocampal representation, without competition from previously acquired appetitive associations.

span.label: remapping poses a stability-plasticity problem: the cells must decide when an environment has changed enough to deserve a new representation
span.quote: If it is true that place cell remapping allows the hippocampus to represent different states of a single environment, then the hippocampus must solve an intriguing stability-plasticity problem ( Grossberg, 1988 ), namely, place cells must somehow decide when the state of a given environment is stable versus when it has changed sufficiently to justify re-representation of that environment by shuffling their preferred firing locations.

span.label: partial remapping may be the compromise - some cells carry the new associations while others preserve what was already learned
span.quote: It is possible that such partial remapping allows the hippocampus to compromise in its attempt to solve the stability-plasticity problem. That is, cells that remap their preferred firing location may allow rapid acquisition of new associations with the context, whereas cells that retain stable firing fields may help to preserve previously learned information about the context.

span.label: what drives remapping is what the animal learned, not the sensory events it received: both groups got the same tone, shock and box
span.quote: These results suggest that place cell remapping in the hippocampus is not strictly determined by the sensory characteristics of the events an animal experiences, but rather what the animal learns about them.

span.label: The study could not determine whether the conditioning-induced remapping is long-lasting or only temporary, because the same cells could not be followed across days.
span.note: what this limits: the persistence of the remapping: BECAUSE OF THE DIFFICULTIES ASSOCIATED WITH RECORDING THE SAME PLACE CELLS OVER MULTIPLE DAYS, WE WERE UNABLE TO ADDRESS THIS QUESTION
span.quote: Because of the difficulties associated with recording the same place cells over multiple days, we were unable to address this question in the present study.

span.label: Behavioural confounds can only be partially ruled out; the authors control for several but concede the list cannot be exhaustive.
span.note: what this limits: every behavioural-confound exclusion in the paper: IT IS NOT POSSIBLE TO CONTROL FOR EVERY POSSIBLE BEHAVIORAL INFLUENCE ON PLACE CELL ACTIVITY - the control set is partial by admission
span.quote: It is not possible to control for every possible behavioral influence on place cell activity, but in this section, we present several analyses of behavioral variables that could possibly account for the remapping observed in the context group.

span.label: The within-session stability control excluded cells that gained or lost a field, so it does not cover the full remapping population.
span.note: what this limits: the within-session stability control specifically: it excluded cells that gained or lost a field, so it does not cover the full population it is used to reassure about
span.quote: Note that this analysis could be performed only on cells that had place fields both before and after conditioning, so gains/losses of field were not included.

span.label: the authors state outright that not every behavioural influence can be controlled, and present the controls as several rather than all
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - not every behavioural influence can be controlled, and the controls are presented as several rather than exhaustive
span.quote: It is not possible to control for every possible behavioral influence on place cell activity, but in this section, we present several analyses of behavioral variables that could possibly account for the remapping observed in the context group.

span.label: whether the remapping lasts is unknown, and the one comparable study found the effect temporary
span.note: what this limits: the durability of the remapping: the one comparable effect WAS TEMPORARY, AND PLACE CELLS EVENTUALLY RESUMED THEIR ORIGINAL FIRING FIELDS, so whether this one lasts is unknown
span.quote: However, this remapping effect was temporary, and place cells eventually resumed their original firing fields. This finding raises the question of whether the context conditioning-induced remapping we observed here is long lasting, or whether it might be only temporary. Because of the difficulties associated with recording the same place cells over multiple days, we were unable to address this question in the present study.

span.label: the paper's own central speculation - that remapping cells are the ones that acquire the association - is declared hard to test
span.note: what this limits: the paper's central speculation, labelled as one: IT IS TEMPTING TO SPECULATE THAT PLACE CELLS THAT REMAP THEIR FIRING LOCATION IN RESPONSE TO A NOVEL REINFORCER ... ARE MORE LIKELY TO BECOME ASSOCIATED WITH THAT REINFORCER
span.quote: It is tempting to speculate that place cells that remap their firing location in response to a novel reinforcer (such as shock) are more likely to become associated with that reinforcer (and thereby support the contextual prediction of that reinforcer) than place cells that do not remap. It would be difficult to test this idea experimentally.

span.label: at the moment the effect is strongest the measurement is impossible: freezing destroys the spatial sampling a place map needs
span.note: what this limits: the period immediately after conditioning, when the effect should be largest and cannot be measured: BECAUSE RATS WERE FREEZING ABOUT ONE-THIRD OF THE TIME ... IT WAS NOT POSSIBLE TO ANALYZE PLACE CELL ACTIVITY BECAUSE OF POOR SAMPLING OF THE ENVIRONMENT
span.quote: Because rats were freezing about one-third of the time during the 10 min immediately after conditioning, it was not possible to analyze place cell activity because of poor sampling of the environment by the rats.

span.label: 53 of 154 recorded cells met inclusion criteria, and four of sixteen rats contributed none
span.note: what this limits: the sample behind every remapping figure: 154 hippocampal cells were recorded and OF THESE, 53 COMPLEX SPIKE CELLS met criteria
span.quote: A total of 154 hippocampal θ and complex spike cells was recorded during fear conditioning from the 16 rats in both groups ( Fig. 3 shows an example an electrode tip placed in the CA1 region of the dorsal hippocampus). Of these, 53 complex spike cells (cued group, n = 27; context group, n = 26) met criteria for inclusion in the present study (see Materials and Methods). Henceforth, we shall refer to these cells as place cells, because all exhibited spatial firing correlates. Two rats from each group had no cells that met criteria for inclusion in the analysis; consequently, the cells included in this study were recorded from six rats in the cued group and six rats in the context group.

span.label: the authors state that the controls are several, not exhaustive - 'It is not possible to control for every possible behavioral influence'
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - IT IS NOT POSSIBLE TO CONTROL FOR EVERY POSSIBLE BEHAVIORAL INFLUENCE ON PLACE CELL ACTIVITY
span.quote: It is not possible to control for every possible behavioral influence on place cell activity, but in this section, we present several analyses of behavioral variables that could possibly account for the remapping observed in the context group.

span.label: the paired versus unpaired contingency design, which holds the stimuli constant and varies only what they predict
span.quote: place cell remapping was more pronounced in rats that primarily learned to fear the training environment (context group) compared with rats that primarily learned to fear the auditory CS (cued group), even though the stimuli (CS, US, and training box) in both tasks were the same

span.label: the stability-plasticity dilemma, imported as the problem the hippocampus must be solving
span.quote: If it is true that place cell remapping allows the hippocampus to represent different states of a single environment, then the hippocampus must solve an intriguing stability-plasticity problem ( Grossberg, 1988 ), namely, place cells must somehow decide when the state of a given environment is stable versus when it has changed sufficiently to justify re-representation of that environment by shuffling their preferred firing locations.

span.label: pixelwise correlation between two rate maps as the measure of whether a representation changed
span.quote: To further quantify the remapping of place cells caused by fear acquisition, we calculated two correlation indices for each place cell—one for the training ( r T ) and one for the control box ( r C )—by computing the pixel-by-pixel correlation between preconditioning and postconditioning place maps (see Materials and Methods). Low r values indicate that the cell remaps its firing field in a given box after conditioning, whereas high r values indicate that the place map remains stable

span.label: place maps built ONLY from periods when the rat was moving
span.note: eliminates: freezing as a direct influence on the place maps - the fear-conditioned group froze far more (92 s against 57 s), and a stationary animal contributes no position samples, so freezing would otherwise shape the map itself
span.quote: However, because place maps included only data from periods when rats were moving (see Materials and Methods), freezing behavior could not have directly influenced our analysis of place maps.

span.label: the post-conditioning session EXTENDED to 12 minutes for the context group against 10 for the cued group
span.note: eliminates: the number of position samples as the difference between groups - more freezing means fewer samples in a fixed session, and a sparser map remaps more readily for purely statistical reasons
span.quote: Furthermore, the duration of the postconditioning place map session in the training box was extended to 12 min for rats in the context group (compared with 10 min for the cued group), so that, despite the increased freezing in the context group, there was no significant difference between groups in the mean number of position samples used to create the place map for this session

span.label: remapping here = a change of firing location across sessions in an UNCHANGED environment, not the classic sense of a change between two different environments
span.quote: However, place cells can change, or remap, their preferred firing locations within a spatial environment, even when the environment itself remains unchanged

span.label: partial remapping = some cells remap and others do not IN THE SAME ANIMAL, so an average over cells describes no cell
span.quote: Although many place cells remapped their firing fields in the training box as a consequence of conditioning, not all of them did. Indeed, even among cells recorded from a single animal, some cells remapped, whereas others did not, a phenomenon that has been referred to as “partial remapping”

span.label: place cell here is a filtered category: 53 of 154 recorded cells that passed three criteria are renamed place cells for the rest of the paper
span.quote: Henceforth, we shall refer to these cells as place cells, because all exhibited spatial firing correlates.

span.label: stable is defined numerically as r > 0.33 between pre and post maps, and is an INCLUSION criterion, not a result
span.quote: Third, to insure that remapping was not caused by movement of the recording electrode, cells had to exhibit a stable (non-remapping; defined as r > 0.33) place field during preconditioning and postconditioning sessions in at least one of the boxes.

span.label: freezing is operationalised as zero tracked movement for at least a third of a second, machine-scored, validated against human observers
span.quote: An episode of freezing was defined as a period during which the rat's movement speed was zero (that is, the animal's tracked position did not change) for a period of ≥⅓ sec.

span.label: claim_type: existence
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: existence — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: We recorded hippocampal place cells in two spatial environments: a training environment in which rats underwent fear conditioning and a neutral control environment. Fear conditioning caused many place cells to alter (or remap) their preferred firing locations in the training environment, whereas most cells remained stable in the control environment. This finding indicates that aversive reinforcement can induce place cell remapping even when the environment itself remains unchanged.

span.label: method: chronic tetrode recording of CA1 place cells in two boxes, before and after paired or unpaired tone-shock conditioning, with pixelwise map correlation
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: While foraging, rats underwent fear conditioning in which an auditory conditioned stimulus (CS) was either paired (cued group; n = 8 rats) or explicitly unpaired (context group; n = 8 rats) with an electric shock as unconditioned stimulus (US).

span.label: phenomenon: place cell remapping - a change of preferred firing location within an unchanged environment
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: hippocampal place cell remapping during fear conditioning — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: However, place cells can change, or remap, their preferred firing locations within a spatial environment, even when the environment itself remains unchanged

span.label: extends → Moita et al. (2003)
span.quote: The data presented in this study were collected concurrently with data reported in a previous study, from the same group of rats ( Moita et al., 2003 ).

span.label: replicates → Rescorla (1968); Phillips and LeDoux (1994)
span.quote: Hence, in accordance with previous studies ( Rescorla, 1968 ; Phillips and LeDoux, 1994 ), we found that rats in the cued group acquired more fear of the CS than of the context (because the CS is the best predictor of shock when it is paired with the US), whereas rats in the context group acquired more fear of the context than of the CS (because the context is the best predictor of shock when the CS and US are unpaired).

span.label: builds-on → Sharp (1999); Eichenbaum (2000)
span.quote: This is consistent with the notion that the hippocampus is not only important for discriminating among different spatial environments, but also for encoding specific temporal or behavioral variables within a single environment ( Sharp, 1999 ; Eichenbaum, 2000 ).

span.label: extends → the literature showing place fields are stable across repeated visits to one environment
span.quote: When a rat first explores a novel environment, hippocampal place cells establish preferred firing locations within that environment ( Wilson and McNaughton, 1993 ), which tend to remain stable during repeated visits to the same environment

span.label: extends → prior reports of remapping when reinforcement location changes
span.quote: However, this remapping effect was temporary, and place cells eventually resumed their original firing fields. This finding raises the question of whether the context conditioning-induced remapping we observed here is long lasting, or whether it might be only temporary. Because of the difficulties associated with recording the same place cells over multiple days, we were unable to address this question in the present study.

span.label: qualifies → the view that the hippocampal code represents the geometry of space
span.quote: In summary, the results of the present study support the view that hippocampal place cells encode not only the geometry of a spatial environment, but also the motivational and behavioral variables that are associated with the environment.

span.label: builds-on → Moita et al. 2003, from the same recordings in the same rats
span.quote: The data presented in this study were collected concurrently with data reported in a previous study, from the same group of rats

span.label: supports → accounts in which the hippocampus encodes behavioural and temporal context within one environment
span.quote: These results suggest that place cell remapping in the hippocampus is not strictly determined by the sensory characteristics of the events an animal experiences, but rather what the animal learns about them.

span.label: remap —operationalised-as→ correlation index
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: low r means the cell remapped, high r means the map held - the whole finding rests on this one number
span.quote: To further quantify the remapping of place cells caused by fear acquisition, we calculated two correlation indices for each place cell—one for the training ( r T ) and one for the control box ( r C )—by computing the pixel-by-pixel correlation between preconditioning and postconditioning place maps (see Materials and Methods). Low r values indicate that the cell remaps its firing field in a given box after conditioning, whereas high r values indicate that the place map remains stable

span.label: remap —operationalised-as→ peak shift
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — a second, independent operationalisation of the same construct, reported alongside the first
span.quote: Field peak shifts were significantly larger in the training than the control box: s training = 13.95 ± 1.78, and s control = 8.76 ± 0.95 (paired t (30) = -2.48; p = 0.02), suggesting that place fields remapped the training box, while remaining stable in the control box.

span.label: place field —operationalised-as→ spatial information
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — one of three joint criteria: peak rate above 1.5 Hz, information above 0.2 bits/spike, at least 50 spikes
span.quote: A cell was considered to have a place field during a given session if its peak in-field firing rate was >1.5 Hz, spatial information content was >0.2 bits/spike, and the cell fired at least 50 spikes during the session

span.label: freezing —operationalised-as→ fear conditioning
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — direction is measure-to-construct: freezing is the read-out of the learning, machine-scored
span.quote: An episode of freezing was defined as a period during which the rat's movement speed was zero (that is, the animal's tracked position did not change) for a period of ≥⅓ sec.

span.label: partial remapping —is-a→ remap
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — a heterogeneous case of it: the population does not act as one, so a mean over cells describes no cell
span.quote: Although many place cells remapped their firing fields in the training box as a consequence of conditioning, not all of them did. Indeed, even among cells recorded from a single animal, some cells remapped, whereas others did not, a phenomenon that has been referred to as “partial remapping”

span.label: movement of the recording electrode —causes→ remap
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — the ARTEFACT that would mimic the finding; excluded by requiring each cell to be stable in at least one box
span.quote: Third, to insure that remapping was not caused by movement of the recording electrode, cells had to exhibit a stable (non-remapping; defined as r > 0.33) place field during preconditioning and postconditioning sessions in at least one of the boxes.

span.label: control box —contrasted-with→ training box
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the same cells in both, so the control environment is a within-cell baseline rather than a separate group
span.quote: The correlation indices were significantly greater in the control box than the training box: r C = 0.59 ± 0.04 and r T = 0.39 ± 0.05 (paired t (41) = 3.15; p = 0.003). This again indicates that place cell remapping was more likely to occur in the training than in the control box.

span.label: contextual fear conditioning —is-a→ fear conditioning
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: While foraging, rats underwent fear conditioning in which an auditory conditioned stimulus (CS) was either paired (cued group; n = 8 rats) or explicitly unpaired (context group; n = 8 rats) with an electric shock as unconditioned stimulus (US).

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · fear conditioning —causes→ remap
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span is the STATISTICS of the effect, not the statement of it - 'Field peak shifts were significantly larger in the training than the control box: s training = 13.95 +/- 1.78, and s control = 8.76 +/- 0.95 (paired t (30) = -2.48; p = 0.02)' - which names one endpoint and carries NO EFFECT CUE, so a `causes` edge on it would fail the gate's causes test today. The replacement is the authors' own sentence for the same result: 'FEAR CONDITIONING CAUSED many place cells to alter (or REMAP) their preferred firing locations in the training environment, whereas most cells remained stable in the control environment.' Both endpoints named, the verb is `caused`, and the control comparison is inside the span. THE NUMBERS ARE NOT LOST - they remain on the record as content_tags and in the retracted span itself, which is why retraction-in-place matters. — status: the paper's own words: suggesting that · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Field peak shifts were significantly larger in the training than the control box: s training = 13.95 ± 1.78, and s control = 8.76 ± 0.95 (paired t (30) = -2.48; p = 0.02), suggesting that place fields remapped the training box, while remaining stable in the control box.

span.label: freezing —causes→ place maps
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — SIGN: destructive. The behaviour that proves the manipulation worked is what prevents measuring its consequence
span.quote: Because rats were freezing about one-third of the time during the 10 min immediately after conditioning, it was not possible to analyze place cell activity because of poor sampling of the environment by the rats.

span.label: within-session —distinct-from→ remap
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: within-session correlation was unchanged and higher than between-session, so the cells built a NEW STABLE map rather than becoming noisy
span.quote: Furthermore, the within-session correlation value in the training box after conditioning is significantly higher than the between-session correlation value in the training box, that is, r POST = 0.56 ± 0.04 and r T = 0.39 ± 0.05 (paired t (41) = -2.20; p = 0.03). These results are in accordance with the interpretation that the conditioning-induced remapping reflects the formation of a stable new map of the training environment.

span.label: place cells —is-a→ complex spike cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: A total of 154 hippocampal θ and complex spike cells was recorded during fear conditioning from the 16 rats in both groups ( Fig. 3 shows an example an electrode tip placed in the CA1 region of the dorsal hippocampus). Of these, 53 complex spike cells (cued group, n = 27; context group, n = 26) met criteria for inclusion in the present study (see Materials and Methods). Henceforth, we shall refer to these cells as place cells, because all exhibited spatial firing correlates. Two rats from each group had no cells that met criteria for inclusion in the analysis; consequently, the cells included in this study were recorded from six rats in the cued group and six rats in the context group.

span.label: spatial uniformity index —part-of→ place maps
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — a control measure on the sampling behind the map, not on the map itself
span.quote: The spatial uniformity index (SUI) was computed as ∑ i = 1, ρ ( p i - 1/ρ) 2 , where index i sums over the ρ adequately sampled pixel bins that were included in both the preconditioning and postconditioning place maps, and p i is the actual percentage of time the rat spent in the i th pixel bin. θ Power.

span.label: fear conditioning —causes→ remap
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Fear conditioning caused many place cells to alter (or remap) their preferred firing locations in the training environment, whereas most cells remained stable in the control environment.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: A two-way ANOVA, testing for main effect of group and main effect of box, revealed no significant effect of group ( F (1) = 0.001; p = 0.97), a significant effect of box ( F (1) = 25.36; p < 0.0001), and no significant interaction ( F (1) = 0.24; p = 0.88).

span.label: post hoc test
span.quote: Post hoc Newman-Keuls t tests showed that, after conditioning, rats in the cued group froze significantly more to the auditory CS than rats in the context group ( p = 0.0006), whereas rats in the context group froze more to the training context than rats in the cued group ( p = 0.04).

span.label: paired t-test
span.quote: The correlation indices were significantly greater in the control box than the training box: r C = 0.59 ± 0.04 and r T = 0.39 ± 0.05 (paired t (41) = 3.15; p = 0.003).

span.label: unpaired t-test
span.quote: Conditioning did not induce any significant change in θ power of the multiunit signal during spike generation by place cells (unpaired t (14) = 1.22; p = 0.24).

span.label: correlation
span.quote: To compute the Pearson product-moment correlation ( r ) between firing rates in the pixels of each map, it was necessary to have the same number of pixels in the preconditioning and postconditioning place maps.

span.label: z-score standardization
span.quote: To compare remapping between the context and cued groups, we computed a Z -score for each cell from both groups.

span.label: paired t test
span.quote: The correlation indices were significantly greater in the control box than the training box: r C = 0.59 ± 0.04 and r T = 0.39 ± 0.05 (paired t (41) = 3.15; p = 0.003). This again indicates that place cell remapping was more likely to occur in the training than in the control box.

span.label: unpaired t
span.quote: We found that the normalized r T was smaller for cells in the context group than the cued group ( Z context = -1.36 ± 0.33 and Z cued = -0.34 ± 0.25; unpaired t (44) = 2.47; p = 0.02), suggesting that remapping of the training box relative to the control box was more pronounced in cells recorded from the context group than the cued group.

span.label: two-way ANOVA
span.quote: Post hoc Newman-Keuls t tests showed that, after conditioning, rats in the cued group froze significantly more to the auditory CS than rats in the context group ( p = 0.0006), whereas rats in the context group froze more to the training context than rats in the cued group

span.label: Newman-Keuls
span.quote: Post hoc Newman-Keuls t tests showed that, after conditioning, rats in the cued group froze significantly more to the auditory CS than rats in the context group ( p = 0.0006), whereas rats in the context group froze more to the training context than rats in the cued group

span.label: Pearson product-moment correlation
span.quote: To further quantify the remapping of place cells caused by fear acquisition, we calculated two correlation indices for each place cell—one for the training ( r T ) and one for the control box ( r C )—by computing the pixel-by-pixel correlation between preconditioning and postconditioning place maps (see Materials and Methods). Low r values indicate that the cell remaps its firing field in a given box after conditioning, whereas high r values indicate that the place map remains stable

span.label: Z -score
span.quote: To compare remapping between the context and cued groups, we computed a Z -score for each cell from both groups. The Z -scores were based on the mean correlation index in the control box for each group, which was used as the expected correlation value, because place fields were most stable in this box.

span.label: Fear conditioning made many CA1 place cells shift, lose or gain their preferred firing locations in the training box, while cells stayed stable in a neutral control box, showing that aversive reinforcement alone can trigger remapping without any change to the environment.
span.quote: Fear conditioning caused many place cells to alter (or remap) their preferred firing locations in the training environment, whereas most cells remained stable in the control environment.

span.label: Pixel-by-pixel correlations between pre- and post-conditioning maps were higher in the control box (0.59) than in the training box (0.39), confirming that remapping was specific to the conditioned environment.
span.quote: The correlation indices were significantly greater in the control box than the training box: r C = 0.59 ± 0.04 and r T = 0.39 ± 0.05 (paired t (41) = 3.15; p = 0.003).

span.label: The peak of the place field moved about 14 cm in the training box versus about 9 cm in the control box after conditioning.
span.quote: Field peak shifts were significantly larger in the training than the control box: s training = 13.95 ± 1.78, and s control = 8.76 ± 0.95 (paired t (30) = -2.48; p = 0.02), suggesting that place fields remapped the training box, while remaining stable in the control box.

span.label: Rats trained with the context as the shock predictor showed more remapping (Z = -1.36) than rats trained with the tone as the predictor (Z = -0.34), tying remapping to learned fear of the environment rather than to the stimuli themselves.
span.quote: We found that the normalized r T was smaller for cells in the context group than the cued group ( Z context = -1.36 ± 0.33 and Z cued = -0.34 ± 0.25; unpaired t (44) = 2.47; p = 0.02), suggesting that remapping of the training box relative to the control box was more pronounced in cells recorded from the context group than the cued group.

span.label: Conditioning changed only where cells fired, not how they fired: peak in-field rate, mean rate, spatial information content and field size were all unchanged in the training box.
span.quote: Despite the increased remapping of place cell firing fields observed in the training box, conditioning did not alter the peak in-field firing rate (paired t (41) = -0.48; p = 0.63), mean firing rate (paired t (41) = -1.08; p = 0.29), mean spatial information content (paired t (41) = -0.78; p = 0.44), or mean size of firing fields (paired t (41) = -0.14; p = 0.89) in the training box.

span.label: Within-session map stability was identical before (r = 0.57) and after (r = 0.56) conditioning, so the low between-session correlation reflects a new stable map rather than cells becoming generally unstable.
span.quote: We found that, in the training box, the within-session correlation after conditioning ( r POST = 0.56 ± 0.04) was not significantly different from within-session correlation before conditioning ( r PRE = 0.57 ± 0.03) (paired t (37) = -0.53; p = 0.60), indicating that conditioning did not affect the within-session stability of place fields.

span.label: Remapping was partial rather than global: within the same rat some cells kept their original firing fields while others moved theirs.
span.quote: Remapping of the training environment in the present study was not complete but partial: some place cells retained the same firing fields before and after fear conditioning, whereas other cells remapped (even in the same rat).

span.label: Freezing rose in the training box after shock but not in the never-shocked control box, and cued rats froze more to the tone while context rats froze more to the training context.
span.quote: Post hoc Newman-Keuls t tests showed that, after conditioning, rats in the cued group froze significantly more to the auditory CS than rats in the context group ( p = 0.0006), whereas rats in the context group froze more to the training context than rats in the cued group ( p = 0.04).

span.label: Theta-band power of the multiunit signal during place-cell spiking was unchanged by conditioning, ruling out an arousal-related theta shift as the explanation for the extra remapping in the context group.
span.quote: Conditioning did not induce any significant change in θ power of the multiunit signal during spike generation by place cells (unpaired t (14) = 1.22; p = 0.24).

span.label: place fields shifted further in the training box than in the control box
span.quote: Field peak shifts were significantly larger in the training than the control box: s training = 13.95 ± 1.78, and s control = 8.76 ± 0.95 (paired t (30) = -2.48; p = 0.02), suggesting that place fields remapped the training box, while remaining stable in the control box.

span.label: map correlation was lower in the training box than the control box, 0.39 against 0.59
span.quote: The correlation indices were significantly greater in the control box than the training box: r C = 0.59 ± 0.04 and r T = 0.39 ± 0.05 (paired t (41) = 3.15; p = 0.003). This again indicates that place cell remapping was more likely to occur in the training than in the control box.

span.label: context-conditioned rats remapped more than cue-conditioned rats, though both received the same tone, shock and box
span.quote: We found that the normalized r T was smaller for cells in the context group than the cued group ( Z context = -1.36 ± 0.33 and Z cued = -0.34 ± 0.25; unpaired t (44) = 2.47; p = 0.02), suggesting that remapping of the training box relative to the control box was more pronounced in cells recorded from the context group than the cued group.

span.label: firing rate, spatial information and field size were unchanged - only the location of firing moved

span.label: remapping is partial - within one animal some cells moved and others did not
span.quote: Although many place cells remapped their firing fields in the training box as a consequence of conditioning, not all of them did. Indeed, even among cells recorded from a single animal, some cells remapped, whereas others did not, a phenomenon that has been referred to as “partial remapping”

span.label: cued rats froze more to the tone and context rats more to the box, confirming what each group had learned

span.label: no group difference in preferred circling direction after conditioning - one rat in the cued group and none in the context group switched
span.quote: To examine this possibility, we measured the ratio of clockwise versus counterclockwise turning movements during the preconditioning and postconditioning sessions, and found that one rat in the cued group and no rats in the context group switched their preferred circling direction after conditioning (no difference between the changes in the ratio of clockwise vs counterclockwise angular velocity was found between the two groups; unpaired t (10) = 1.63; p = 0.13). Thus, changes in circling direction probably did not contribute to place cell remapping.

span.quote: The hippocampus contains place cells that fire preferentially when a rat visits specific locations within a spatial environment ( O'Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971 ).

span.quote: An episode of freezing was defined as a period during which the rat's movement speed was zero (that is, the animal's tracked position did not change) for a period of ≥⅓ sec.

span.quote: A cell was considered to have a place field during a given session if its peak in-field firing rate was >1.5 Hz, spatial information content was >0.2 bits/spike, and the cell fired at least 50 spikes during the session (see Table 1 for mean firing properties of place cells).

span.quote: Spatial uniformity index. The spatial uniformity index (SUI) was computed as ∑ i = 1, ρ ( p i - 1/ρ) 2 , where index i sums over the ρ adequately sampled pixel bins that were included in both the preconditioning and postconditioning place maps, and p i is the actual percentage of time the rat spent in the i th pixel bin.

span.label: stability-plasticity problem
span.quote: If it is true that place cell remapping allows the hippocampus to represent different states of a single environment, then the hippocampus must solve an intriguing stability-plasticity problem ( Grossberg, 1988 ), namely, place cells must somehow decide when the state of a given environment is stable versus when it has changed sufficiently to justify re-representation of that environment by shuffling their preferred firing locations.

span.label: CS-US contingency (paired cued group vs explicitly unpaired context group)
span.term: CS-US contingency (paired cued group vs explicitly unpaired context group)
span.quote: While foraging, rats underwent fear conditioning in which an auditory conditioned stimulus (CS) was either paired (cued group; n = 8 rats) or explicitly unpaired (context group; n = 8 rats) with an electric shock as unconditioned stimulus (US).

span.label: place map correlation index (remapping)

span.label: freezing behavior
span.quote: Fear learning was assessed by automated scoring of freezing behavior, a standard index of conditioned fear ( Blanchard and Blanchard, 1969 ).

span.quote: To compensate for different levels of freezing behavior between groups, analyses of place maps included only spikes and position samples from periods when rats were moving at a speed of at least 18 cm/sec (see Results).

span.quote: A total of 154 hippocampal θ and complex spike cells was recorded during fear conditioning from the 16 rats in both groups ( Fig. 3 shows an example an electrode tip placed in the CA1 region of the dorsal hippocampus).
